result.title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation
result.summary: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. The positive estimates determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases. In stochastic point-mass docking experiments, most failures occurred in the final docking phase, whereas the largest completion gain occurred in the preceding channel phase; gain-based allocation improved completion over allocation proportional to failure counts and, in a variant with a longer approach, over uniform allocation at half of the budget. In simulated bimanual robotic assembly, the completion-gain estimates were positive only for insertion and release, although few failures occurred during release; in a second assembly configuration, a residual policy trained in the release phase improved completion from held-out states at the start of release by 16.9%.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究多阶段模仿策略中残差强化学习的预算分配，提出「完成增益」指标，把一次修正对整任务成功概率的影响分解为「到达该阶段的概率」与「条件改善」，并用配对轨迹估计，据此决定修正哪些动作分量、各阶段如何分配训练回合。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「失败最多的阶段未必是最值得修正的阶段」与按增益分配回合预算的思路，可能启发 LVR 中多步 latent 推理的贡献分配与计算预算/停止决策评价，可供核查如何将增益估计迁移为对推理步骤或状态更新的信用度量。
